items.name: Westmoreland County state dog warden (PA Dept. of Agriculture, Bureau of Dog Law Enforcement)
items.what_to_use_it_for: Call the Westmoreland County warden when you find a loose dog or have lost one. Wardens pick up stray dogs and take them to shelters.

items.name: PA Dept. of Agriculture Region 4 office (covers Westmoreland County)
items.what_to_use_it_for: Call here to reach state dog law staff if you can't get through to the county dog warden.

items.name: Animal Protectors of Allegheny Valley
items.what_to_use_it_for: The shelter in town: call first when a dog or cat goes missing or turns up in New Kensington, Arnold or Lower Burrell.

items.name: Hoffman Kennels (contracted animal control officer)
items.what_to_use_it_for: If your dog went missing in Lower Burrell, call Hoffman Kennels, the city's listed animal control officer, to ask whether it was picked up. In Arnold, ask police whether the dog catcher has it.

items.name: Humane Society of Westmoreland County
items.what_to_use_it_for: Report a lost or found pet to the county humane society and check whether it has taken the animal in.

items.name: Kiski Valley Cat & Kitten Rescue
items.what_to_use_it_for: For cats: a Kiski Valley cat rescue near 15068 to ask about a found cat or kitten or to check for a lost cat.

items.name: New Kensington Police Department (non-emergency)
items.what_to_use_it_for: Report a lost dog or cat, or a loose one you found, in New Kensington.

items.name: Arnold Police Department (non-emergency)
items.what_to_use_it_for: Report a lost or found pet in Arnold and ask whether the city's contracted dog catcher picked up an animal.

items.name: Lower Burrell Police Department (non-emergency)
items.what_to_use_it_for: Report a lost or found pet in Lower Burrell.

items.name: Westmoreland County Public Safety non-emergency line
items.what_to_use_it_for: Call after hours to report a loose dog or another non-emergency animal problem when you can't reach local police.

items.name: AVETS (Allegheny Veterinary Emergency Trauma & Specialty)
items.what_to_use_it_for: The closest 24/7 emergency vet: take an injured found or lost pet here, and call to ask whether an injured animal was brought in.

items.name: BluePearl Pet Hospital Pittsburgh North (formerly Pittsburgh Veterinary Specialty & Emergency Center)
items.what_to_use_it_for: A backup 24-hour emergency hospital for an injured pet if AVETS isn't an option.

items.name: AAHA Universal Pet Microchip Lookup
items.what_to_use_it_for: After a vet or shelter scans a found pet, enter the chip number here to find out which registry holds the owner's contact details.

items.name: Westmoreland County Treasurer, dog licenses
items.address: 2 North Main Street, Suite 110, Greensburg, PA 15601
items.what_to_use_it_for: Buy or renew a county dog license, and call about a Westmoreland license tag on a found dog.

items.name: PA Dept. of Agriculture, Dog Licenses
items.what_to_use_it_for: Look up the state dog-license rules. A current license tag is one of the fastest ways to get a lost dog home.

items.name: PawBoost lost & found pets
items.what_to_use_it_for: Post a free lost or found alert and search pets already reported near 15068.

items.name: Petco Love Lost
items.what_to_use_it_for: Upload a photo of a lost or found dog or cat to match it against a national database, including shelter pets.

items.name: Find Toby in PA
items.what_to_use_it_for: Follow its free statewide step-by-step guides for a lost pet (/lost-pet) or a found pet (/found-pet), and read its summary of PA law (/pa-law).

tips.tip: Found a dog: promptly call the police, animal control or the dog warden so the dog can go to a licensed stray-hold facility, as PA law requires. A stray dog must be held at least 48 hours in an approved kennel before ownership can legally transfer or it can be adopted, so the owner has a window to reclaim it.
Lost a pet: call local shelters, animal control and vet clinics to ask whether your pet was brought in, and keep checking back instead of calling only once.

Tell your pet's microchip company it is missing. The company can alert shelters and vets in the area and contact you if someone reports finding the pet. A chip only helps if your contact details on file are current.

Search on foot and put up flyers. Walk the neighborhood, knock on doors, and look under decks, sheds, porches and thick shrubs. Post flyers at vet offices, groomers, pet stores, dog parks, grocery and convenience stores, gas stations and laundromats.

Post the pet on both Petco Love Lost (free photo matching against lost, found and shelter pets, with cross-posting to Nextdoor and Ring Neighbors) and PawBoost (free local email alert, regional Facebook post and flyer).
Keep your dog licensed. Pennsylvania requires a license once a dog is 3 months old, and a current tag lets a warden or shelter trace the owner quickly.
